item.title: How one antibiotic morning-after pill came to be widely available in San Francisco
item.description: An antibiotic morning-after pill has been shown to be effective for preventing STIs among gay men, but some doctors worry about antibiotic resistance. This story discusses STIs and their symptoms.
item.content:encoded: An antibiotic morning-after pill has been shown to be effective for preventing STIs among gay men, but some doctors worry about antibiotic resistance. This story discusses STIs and their symptoms.

item.title: Don't be scared: Being afraid is outright fun, and maybe useful
item.description: Listeners of NPR's Weekend Edition Sunday may already know that host Ayesha Rascoe loves horror. But why do scream queens (and kings) like her like what's frightening? The answer may surprise you.

item.title: She was a global star: Teen bikes 700 miles carrying injured dad. Where is she now?
item.description: Her epic ride — carrying her injured dad on her $20 hot pink bicycle — made headlines. Promises were made — financial help, training for a cycling career, even a movie deal. Were any of them kept?

item.title: Sweating the details: Sauna's potential health benefits draw scientists' interest
item.description: A group of international researchers is pushing to rigorously study the potential health benefits of sauna and other heat therapies. They hope to bring scientific legitimacy to the age-old practices.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Ongoing lawsuits allege GLP-1s can cause serious harm. But we don't know how often
item.description: Scant data about serious adverse effects makes it harder to answer scientific and legal questions about how often the drugs might cause serious harm like blindness or pancreatitis.

item.title: Did Russia play by the rules in reporting lab worker's death?
item.description: A global treaty signed by 197 countries — including Russia — requires reporting any death that could be a sign of an outbreak to come.

item.title: ChatGPT for Teens has special safeguards. A watchdog group finds most don't work
item.description: A study from Common Sense Media says most safeguards in ChatGPT for Teens failed. The chatbot talks to teens like a friend and doesn't alert parents when users talk about self-harm and suicide.
